headline: pki.path.build can search from a trust anchor toward the leaf, not only from the leaf toward an anchor.
summary: pki.path.build accepts an opts.direction of "forward" (the default, unchanged), "reverse", or "auto". Reverse building (RFC 4158 sec. 3.1) searches from a trust anchor down to the leaf, which is narrower when the anchor set is small and the leaf's issuer options fan out, such as a leaf with no authority key identifier or a cross-certified bridge mesh. Auto picks the direction by comparing the first-hop candidate counts. Reverse building reuses the same candidate pool, cycle-detecting visited-set, work caps, and validate gate as forward building, so the direction changes only the search order, never which paths are accepted: every assembled path is handed to pki.path.validate, and the anchor is excluded from the returned path. Reverse building is pool-only and does not combine with fetchAia.

Added: pki.path.build accepts opts.direction: "forward" (default), "reverse" (search from a trust anchor toward the leaf, RFC 4158 sec. 3.1), or "auto" (pick by first-hop fan-out).
